fatal_errors: The proposed method is mechanical alloying, whereas the target method is liquid-metal dealloying by immersion of directionally segregated WTaVTi in molten Cu.
The hypothesis incorrectly expects a homogeneous RHEA–Cu solid solution despite the central thermodynamic constraint of strong Cu immiscibility with W, Ta, and V.

It omits selective removal of Ti-rich interdendritic regions, Cu replacement, bicontinuous directional architecture, and formation of the W-rich passivating interlayer responsible for microstructural stability.
The milling parameters, grain-size predictions, baseline, and hardness threshold are unsupported by cited evidence and do not correspond to the reported system.
The proposed experiment does not directly test millimeter-scale Cu penetration, selective elemental exchange, interfacial passivation, thermal transport, or irradiation response.
explanation: The response only aligns at the broad level of addressing an RHEA–Cu processing challenge. It does not reconstruct the reported liquid-metal dealloying route at 1200 °C for 96 h or its mechanism: preferential Ti–Cu exchange in connected Ti/V-rich channels, retention of W/Ta/V-rich ligaments, and arrest of further reaction by an approximately 300 nm W-rich interlayer. Instead, it proposes unsupported mechanical-alloying conditions and a homogeneous solid solution that conflicts with the stated positive heats of mixing. Its predicted fine-grained microstructure and mechanical benefits do not match the demonstrated directionally aligned bicontinuous RHEA–Cu composite or the thermal and helium-irradiation outcomes. Although the comparative experiment is nominally falsifiable, its arbitrary grain-size and hardness criteria do not discriminate the target mechanism.
